newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka '96 budget deficit up to 9 pct GDP-ADB.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka '96 budget deficit up to 9 pct GDP-ADB.

text.p: Sri Lanka's 1996 budget deficit rose to nine percent of gross domestic product (GDP) against 8.4 percent in 1995 due to an upswing in defence expenditure, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Thursday.
The Manila-based bank said in its annual report Sri Lanka had planned to reduce its budget deficit to 7.8 percent of GDP last year.

However, a rise of 40 percent in defence expenditure, the doubling of a wheat subsidy and a slowdown in revenues due to an easing of industrial activity resulted in the deficit rising to nine percent.

"The deficit was contained at this level only through cutbacks in expenditure and increases in tax rates," it said. The report said expenditure was controlled by delays in the implementation of projects.
The bank said that one of the key reasons for the shortfall in budgetary revenue was the slow progress of privatisation.

"The rate of privatisation picked up early in 1995, and 18 enterprises were scheduled for privatisation in 1996. However, in the first nine months of 1996, mainly because of the civil war, only nine privatisations occurred, mostly of plantations," it said.

The war between government forces and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, is now in its 14th year.
